results.title: The Regency Of Algiers
results.creator: Thomas J. Bryan, Claude/Anthropic
results.description: The Regency of Algiers: Patterns of Power (1516–1830) is an analytical case study examining how an order of power was founded, dressed, and held across three centuries . The study follows the state's trajectory from the seizure of Algiers by the corsair brothers Aruj and Khayr al-Din , through its submission to the Ottoman sultan and the eventual rise of the janissary corporation , to the capitulation of the Kasba to a French army on July 5, 1830 . Relying on primary administrative records, consular testimonies, eyewitness accounts, and period inscriptions , the work investigates an order whose revenue ran through maritime and state chokepoints , governed by a corporation that recruited free adult volunteers abroad while barring native Algerians from its pay registers and highest ranks . The volume explores the mechanics of an institutional arrangement where individual titles—such as places on the pay register, prize shares, and farmed offices—were strictly non-heritable and died with their holders , yet the corporate system itself endured . Rather than treating the Regency simply through the conventional lens of a "pirate state," the study details its administrative realities: the extraction of surplus via monopolies, tribute, and escheat ; the dual claims of holy war and diplomatic treaty under Ottoman safe-conduct ; the complete separation between local religious formation and state governance ; and the structural forces that eventually hollowed the order prior to the 1830 conquest .

results.title: Captives and Corsairs: France and Slavery in the Early Modern Mediterranean
creator: Gillian Weiss
results.description: Captives and Corsairs uncovers a forgotten story in the history of relations between the West and Islam: three centuries of Muslim corsair raids on French ships and shores and the resulting captivity of tens of thousands of French subjects and citizens in North Africa. Through an analysis of archival materials, writings, and images produced by contemporaries, the book fundamentally revises our picture of France's emergence as a nation and a colonial power, presenting the Mediterranean as an essential vantage point for studying the rise of France. It reveals how efforts to liberate slaves from North Africa shaped France's perceptions of the Muslim world and of their own Frenchness. From around 1550 to 1830, freeing these captives evolved from an expression of Christian charity to a method of state building and, eventually, to a rationale for imperial expansion. Captives and Corsairs thus advances new arguments about the fluid nature of slavery and firmly links captive redemption to state formation-and in turn to the still vital ideology of liberatory conquest.

results.description: T he galley as a warship was so particularly suited to the geographical features of the M editerranean region that its essential characteristics changed little in two thousand years. T he advantage of the oared vessel was that it could move even in the calm w eather that bedevilled sea travel in the M editerranean. A standard galley possessed two masts retaining lateen (triangular) sails, and was propelled by twenty-five to thirty oars per side. Its narrow hull was just wide enough to fit benches for three or four oarsm en per oar, separated by a central walkway. T he vessel, which lay less than a m etre above the water-line in the centre, had an upraised stern containing com m and and steering functions and a raised bow platform for artillery and storage. All these characteristics enhanced its m anoeuv­ rability, enabling it to circle its target and ‘b ite’ it a t the right spot (the side of ano ther oared vessel, the bow or stern o f a roundship). A com m on but not universal feature was the bronze spur on the bow tha t hooked on to an enem y ship and provided simultaneously a walkway for the boarding party .1 T h e vessel had such shallow draught that it could operate close to shore, or be beached with no difficulty. T hus, the galley served better a military function than a com m ercial one. Built in a similar m anner in Barcelona, Venice and Constantinople, galleys from all over the M editerranean were used side-by-side by their captors and sometimes changed hands several times.

results.title: The Barbary Corsairs: Warfare in the Mediterranean, 1480-1580
creator: Jacques Heers
Jonathan North
results.description: The Barbary Corsairs first appeared to terrorise shipping in the 16th century. These Muslim pirates sailed out of the ports of North Africa and, acting as officers of the sprawling Ottoman empire, plundered the trading routes of the Mediterranean and sowed horror in the hearts of Christians everywhere. The most famous and powerful were the Barbarossa brothers, sons of a renegade Christian. The true founders of the Algiers regency, they initially preyed on fishing vessels or defenceless merchantmen before growing bolder and embarking upon more brazen expeditions, - attacking fortified ports and cities; raiding and kidnapping inhabitants of the African coast; and hunting ships from the Christian nations. In this newly translated book, Jacques Heers follows the extraordinary exploits of the brothers, and those of other corsairs and profiteers, set against the turbulent backdrop of trade, commerce and conflict throughout the Mediterranean during the 14th-16th centuries. It's an enthralling adventure, robustly written, and it brings to life an age when travel and trade were perilous enterprises.

results.title: The Role of Corsairs in the Mediterranean in the Early Modern Period
creator: Martín Richter
results.description: Die Arbeit beschreibt eine Nomenklatur zu den Begriffen Pirat, Korsar, Renegat, sowie anderen Begriffen, die mit Piraten in Verbindung stehen. Durch die Analyse der Situation im Mittelmeer in der Frühen Neuzeit wird der wissenschaftliche Wert der Terminologien unterstrichen. Durch einen Gegenüberstellung der Sekundärliteratur wird diese Terminologie mit Unterstützung von Analysen übersetzter Quellen erarbeitet. Ein besonderes Augenmerk wird auf die Renegaten gelegt, die durch Individualhistorien genauer betrachtet werden. Die Theorie der Entangled History wird analysiert, um zu zeigen, dass es zwischen Europa und dem Osmanischen Reich einen Austausch gab, der dem propagierten Diskurs der Zeit widerspricht. Eine Analyse der Rolle der Religion in Zusammenhang mit Korsaren und vor allem Renegaten soll dabei aufzeigen, dass die Konvertierung hauptsächlich von Pragmatik geleitet war. Ein weiterer Aspekt gilt der Gegenüberstellung von Christlichen und Muslimischen Korsaren, die anhand von Politik, Wirtschaft und Kultur verglichen werden.

creator: Noel Malcolm
results.description: In the second half of the sixteenth century, most of the Christian states of Western Europe were on the defensive against a Muslim superpower - the Empire of the Ottoman sultans. There was violent conflict, from raiding and corsairing to large-scale warfare, but there were also many forms of peaceful interaction across the surprisingly porous frontiers of these opposing power-blocs. Agents of Empire describes the paths taken through the eastern Mediterranean and its European hinterland by members of a Venetian-Albanian family, almost all of them previously invisible to history. They include an archbishop in the Balkans, the captain of the papal flagship at the Battle of Lepanto, the power behind the throne in the Ottoman province of Moldavia, and a dragoman (interpreter) at the Venetian embassy in Istanbul. Through the life-stories of these adventurous individuals over three generations, Noel Malcolm casts the world between Venice, Rome and the Ottoman Empire in a fresh light, illuminating subjects as diverse as espionage, diplomacy, the grain trade, slave-ransoming and anti-Ottoman rebellion. He describes the conflicting strategies of the Christian powers, and the extraordinarily ambitious plans of the sultans and their viziers. Few works since Fernand Braudel's classic account of the sixteenth-century Mediterranean, published more than sixty years ago, have ranged so widely through this vital period of Mediterranean and European history. A masterpiece of scholarship as well as story-telling, Agents of Empire builds up a panoramic picture, both of Western power-politics and of the interrelations between the Christian and Ottoman worlds.

The fleet’s unannounced arrival prompted two days of urgent and complex shuttle diplomacy between the Neapolitan flagship, the Pasha’s Castle (the seat of government) and the Consulates of Great Britain, France, Tuscany and Naples. After two days, and two hours before sunset, when these diplomatic efforts had clearly failed, the fleet opened fire, causing little or no damage to its main target, the Pasha’s Castle, or the town, the land and sea fortifications, or the Tripoline corsair fleet still riding at anchor just outside the large, natural harbour. During the next two days of strong north-easterly gales (August 24 and 25) the Neapolitan fleet was inactive. But even when the weather from August 26 allowed three fine days for bombardment by the fleet’s three or four large gunboats, their exploding bombs (although undoubtedly alarming) caused but slight damage. The other warships failed to come effectively into action with massive broadsides firing heavy round shot, probably because they were too far out to sea, and thus out of range. Then, early on 28 August, nearly a week after its arrival, and with no discernible diplomatic or military achievement, the fleet, “to the great surprise of all”, was seen sailing off northwards, never to return. results.description: Between shortly before midnight of the 24th and early morning of the 25th of September 1679, the life of French corsair Hugues Creveliers, leader of the most important corsair company active in the Aegean sea in the 1670s, came to an inglorious end off the coast of Astypalaia, due to the blowing up of his ship by a member of his crew. In the last part of this study we examine the role of the bay of Vathy in the corsair raids, since this is most likely where the explosion of Creveliers' ship took place. This particular bay has similar traits to other anchorages in the Cycladic islands where we know that corsairs repaired their ships, since they had built small forts of batteries at the narrow entrances to these lairs so that no enemy ship could approach. results.description: When Paul I came to the throne in 1796, Malta and Russia had long had a common enemy. It was the Ottoman Empire, its Muslim Turks, and its Barbary corsairs. Unlike Malta, a central Mediterranean archipelago with well-protected, deep-water harbours, Russia had been a largely landlocked country whose territorial expansion historically had tended to be across internal frontiers, from Kiev to Muscovy to Kazan. With the advent of Peter I, however, and especially after his declaration of war against Turkey and the acquisition of the Black Sea port of Azov in 1696, Russia began to nurture a naval and maritime policy. Paul I's keen interest in Malta and its Catholic, aristocratic order of chivalry, must be seen in the light of a string of earlier acquaintances, overtures and schemes of mutual interest between the Czars of Russia, on one hand, and the Knights of Malta, on the other. Two of his best known predecessors, Peter I (1672-1725) and Catherine II (1729-1796), already had set their sights on Malta, its knights and, not least, its famous fleet. Given the new-found commitment to naval and maritime undertakings, Petrine Russia now had an ideological as well as a strategic shared interest with the Mediterranean headquarters of the anti-Turkish, anti-Muslim crusaders.

citation_title: Mediterranean Voyages : The Archaeology of Island Colonisation and Abandonment
citation_abstract: Islands are ideal case studies for exploring social connectivity, episodes of colonisation, abandonment, and alternating phases of cultural interaction and isolation. Their societies display different attitudes toward the land and the sea, which in turn cast light on group identities. This volume advances theoretical discussions of island archaeology by offering a comparative study of the archaeology of colonisation, abandonment, and resettlement of the Mediterranean islands in prehistory. This comparative and thematic study encourages anthropological reflections on the archaeology of the islands, ultimately focusing on people rather than geographical units, and specifically on the relations between islanders, mainlanders, and the creation of islander identities. This volume has significance for scholars interested in Mediterranean archaeology, as well as those interested more broadly in colonisation and abandonment.

citation_abstract: Bu makale, özellikle şarap ticaretinin rolüne odaklanarak, Palaiologos Dönemi'nde Doğu Akdeniz'de ekonomik birliğin kurulmasını incelemektedir. Çeşitli bölgelerin deniz yolları ve ticaret ağları aracılığıyla birbirlerine nasıl bağlandıklarını ve uyumlu bir ekonomik sisteme nasıl katkıda bulunduklarını araştırmaktadır. Çalışma, toprak sahipleri, köylüler ve tüccarların dâhil olduğu bir nakit ürün olarak şarap üretiminin önemini vurgulamaktadır. Farklı sınıflarda üretilen şarap, günlük tüketimin yanı sıra dini ve sosyal törenlerde de önemli bir rol oynamış ve farklı toplumsal katmanlara hitap etmiştir. Ayrıca bu çalışma, Girit Malmsey ticaretinin ekonomik inceliklerini ortaya koyarak, Akdeniz'de aranan bir meta olarak büyük önemini gözler önüne sermektedir. Tarihi kaynakları ve bilimsel araştırmaları analiz eden bu çalışma, şarap ticaretinin karmaşık dinamiklerine ışık tutarak bölgeler arası ticareti ve kültürel alışverişi kolaylaştırmadaki rolünü vurgulamaktadır. Bulgular, siyasi bölünmüşlüğe rağmen Doğu Akdeniz'in Palaiologoslar Dönemi'nde, geniş ticaret ağları ve şarap ticaretinin öne çıkması sayesinde ekonomik bir bütünlük oluşturduğunu göstermektedir. Bu araştırma, dönemin ekonomik yapısının ve Akdeniz tarihi üzerindeki kalıcı etkisinin anlaşılmasına katkıda bulunmaktadır.
